title: Mapwork: grid references, bearings and distance

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Finding places with grid references, giving directions and bearings, and measuring distances on a large-scale map.

blocks.heading: Grid references
blocks.text: Read the easting first, along the bottom of the map, then the northing, up the side: "along the corridor, then up the stairs". A four-figure reference names the square by the lines at its bottom-left corner. A six-figure reference adds a third figure to each, the tenths of the way across the square, so a point halfway across square 4665 and three-tenths of the way up is 465653.

blocks.heading: Directions, bearings and distance
blocks.text: A compass direction is a point of the compass, such as north-east. A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from grid north: east is 090°, south is 180°. To measure a distance, follow the route with the straight edge of a sheet of paper, then lay it on the scale line. On a map of scale 1:50 000, 1 cm on the map is 0.5 km on the ground.

notes: Structural exemplar. Take its shape, not its length: your word budget is in the work order.
